items.title: Supreme Court directs Delhi lawyers bodies to work out women's representation in their governing bodies
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) and bar bodies of the district courts in the national capital to jointly work out a “structured” and “institutionalised” mechanism for representation of women in their governing bodies for the 2027 Bar elections [Fozia Rahman vs. Bar Council of Delhi and Anr.]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed that the Coordination Committee of All District Court Bar Associations of Delhi, in consultation with the DHCBA and other bar bodies, to come out with a proposal reflecting an "all-acceptable solution." The Court granted six weeks for consultations to ensure that any impediments or bottlenecks arising during deliberations are discussed and resolved well in time. The Bench told the DHCBA that the matter was one of its leadership, statesmanship, stewardship and "a question of prestige." The Court also expressed confidence that the coordination committee would arrive at a workable solution. items.title: Delhi HC says Karni Sena president free to move around but participation in protest must be as per law
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday observed that Rashtriya Karni Sena President Dr Raj Shekhawat is free to move around, but if he wants to take part in a protest against UGC's equity regulations, the same shall be in accordance with law. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Vikas Mahajan made the observations while hearing a habeas corpus plea filed by Shekhawat against his alleged house arrest. Advocate Lokesh Bhardwaj appeared for Shekhawat and told the Court that Shekhawat was illegally detained by the Delhi Police and placed under house arrest to prevent him from leading a protest against the UGC's norms. Meanwhile, the Delhi Police told the Bench that Shekhawat was not arrested in any case. However, the police added that there is an apprehension that he may go to Jantar Mantar for protest. After considering the submissions, the Bench said that since Shekhawat has not been detained, he is free to move around. items.title: 10 Karnataka Bills passed without debate as BJP-JD(S) protest over Nagendra continues
items.summary: The Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Council on Monday, August 24, passed 10 Bills without debate as BJP and JD(S) members continued their protest demanding the resignation of Minister B Nagendra, who has been chargesheeted in the alleged embezzlement of funds in the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation. The passage of the Bills came on the final day of the monsoon session, which was scheduled to continue until Tuesday and Thursday but ended abruptly with both Houses being adjourned sine die. The 10-day monsoon session was the first after D K Shivakumar became Chief Minister. However, amid the continuing protests, the legislature was adjourned sine die on Monday evening, bringing the session to an end two days ahead of schedule. Among the Bills passed was the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (Amendment) Bill, Karnataka Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Bill, Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Second Amendment) Bill, Karnataka Industries (Facilitation) (Amendment) Bill, Karnataka Sakala Services (Amendment)

District Judge Atul Ahlawat of Saket Courts on August 20 ruled that the wife failed to prove that her husband's affair partner actively induced or encouraged the breakdown of the marriage. The Court found no direct evidence to show that the other woman had induced the husband to leave his wife. It added that the wife's suspicions and information allegedly received from a driver, who died before he could testify, could not take the place of proof. “ Merely because two consenting adults had entered into a consensual sexual relationship outside the marriage and it led to the birth of a child, does not in itself establish the requirements with respect to the ingredients of the present tort of AoA ,” the Court said. items.title: Understanding the intelligence pyramid: Why most businesses know everything and do nothing?
items.summary: In every consequential field of human endeavour, whether in the boardroom, the courtroom, or on the trading floor, one resource has consistently separated those who prevail from those who do not. The resource is intelligence: information that has been processed, placed in context, and converted into a decision within the window in which that decision still counts. Military history makes the point plainly. The intelligence failures that determined the outcomes of wars were rarely failures of collection; the signals were usually present. What failed was the architecture to convert those signals into understanding, and the discipline to act before the moment passed. Corporate history repeats the lesson, and increasingly, so does the law. When a regulator, a court, or a shareholder examines how an organisation behaved before a loss crystallised, the question is seldom whether the information existed. It is whether the organisation recognised what it held and converted that knowledge into a reasoned, recorded decision, or allowed it to travel no further than the report in which it arrived.
